content.value:
The Chargers (1-9) are back at home this week to face the Patriots (5-5) in the hopes of earning their first win inside SoFi Stadium this season. New England is coming off their bye week and have had two weeks to get backup quarterback Tommy DeVito up to speed in the wake of Drake Maye’s injury that will sideline him until at least the postseason.

Two inexperienced backup quarterbacks are not what most fans would like to watch during a football game in Novemeber, but sometimes that’s the reality of the NFL. To look at this from a more positive view, fans of both teams will get their first look at their backups to see what their team truly has behind the starters. This could be a good or bad experience, but overall everyone will leave the day more enlightened! That’s a win, right?

The Chargers are playing for nothing but their own prides while the Patriots are still fighting to right the ship and hopefully find a way into the postseason. Both teams have dealt with injuries this year to impact players, and that goes beyond the quarterback spot. Wideout A.J. Brown will not play in this one which is a good thing for a Chargers defense that could be without half of their starting unit on Sunday.

Being short-handed like that never fun, and it makes the hopes that DJU could somehow lead them to an improbable victory even slimmer.

But hey, when everyone is going poorly, all you can do is throw your hands up and try to enjoy the ride.

Below are the three things I’ll be watching closely when these teams take the field on Sunday.

1.) Which backup QB will prevail in this underwhelming tale of the tape?

Just like everyone would have predicted before the season began, the quarterback matchup for the Chargers’ rematch with the Patriots is D.J. Uiagalelei and Tommy DeVito. Better grab your popcorn!

Uiagalelei is a second-year UDFA who only has one seven career pass attempts to his name, all of which came in garbage time against the Texans. He completed only two passes in those snaps, but one did go for a touchdown to Derius Davis.

DeVito comes into this game with eight starts under his belt and nine career touchdown passes to four inteceptions. He has not started a game this year, but has thrown for 132 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in three appearances.

With two inexperienced quarterbacks on the field, you can fully expected both defenses to rev up their pass rush early and often to rattle them as soon as possible.

2.) How will Mike McDaniel change the offense around DJU?

It’s not like the Chargers were throwing the ball all that much before Justin Herbert’s concussion, but it’s likely to be even less without the Chargers starting quarterback.

The Chargers have run the football at least 30 times in each of their last three games. They rushed for 138 yards against the Texans, 160 against the Ravens, and 158 against the Texans. Omarion Hampton scored against the Ravens but Herbert has the other two rushing touchdowns over those three games with one coming against the Ravens and Jets, apiece.

Uiagalelei also has the athleticism to produce on the ground if he wants, and it’ll be interesting to see if McDaniel uses him in a similar way as Herbert as of late.

In all honesty, I would not be shocked if the Chargers set a new season-high for rushing attempts in a game against the Patriots. It would minimize the pressure on DJU and keep the play-action game alive to make sure the defense can’t get to overeager against such a green player.

If all goes well, maybe we get Hampton’s second 100-yard game of the season, as well.

3.) How will the Chargers defense handle playing without numerous starters?

The Chargers defense looked the worst they have all year against the Jets in a game where starting linebacker Daiyan Henley and cornerback Tarheeb Still were sidelined with injuries. Star safety Derwin James has also missed the past month and isn’t coming back for multiple weeks while on IR.

As of Friday morning, the Chargers were on pace to play a number of backups on defense thanks to a laundry list of a injury report through the first two practices.

Henley and Still have not practiced in any capacity and will likely miss another week. Joining them on the sidelines through Wednesday and Thursday were edge rushers Tuli Tuipulotu and Akheem Mesidor, and defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson. If all of those latter three do not practice in some way on Friday, the Chargers could play the Patriots without half of their starting defense.

That’s not great, Bob!

The secondary is already a shallow group and now the front seven gets even thinner if two of the team’s top three edge rushers are forced to miss Sunday. It would be Bud Dupree starting opposite Khalil Mack and Caleb Murphy as the No. 3 pass rusher.

Once again, the linebacker rotation will feature Del’Shawn Phillips, Marlowe Wax, Troy Dye, and veteran Denzel Perryman. No studs by any means and they’ll have to do better at stopping the run game which New England will likely try to lean on, especially seeing how consistent the Jets were at getting chunks in Week 11.

Looking at this injury report, the Chargers will have to get a number of depth pieces to play above themselves in over to avoid falling to 1-10.

The Chargers began their week of practice today in preparation for the Patriots and it came with one of the most concerning injury reports in recent memory.

Wednesday’s report featured 13 players, all of which were listed as a DNP. That group of 13 players included Justin Herbert (concussion), linebacker Daiyan Henley (knee), edge rushers Tuli Tuipulotu (ankle) and Akheem Mesidor (ankle), and cornerback Tarheeb Still (ankle). Both Henley and Still did not play against the Jets on Sunday and neither look to have progressed much with an entire week off.

The rest of the players who sat out Wednesday were cornerback Deane Leonard (groin), edge rusher Khalil Mack (veteran’s rest day), running back Keaton Mitchell (knee), tight end David Njoku (shoulder), defensive tackle Teair Tart (rest day), wideout Brenen Thompson (hamstring), defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson (knee), and safety Kendall Williamson (calf).

The Chargers are 1-9 heading into this week’s matchup with the 5-5 Patriots. After losing to a fellow AFC East member in the Jets this past Sunday, the Bolts will look to get right again against another team who recently lost their starting quarterback.

Drake Maye will not be out there for the Patriots offense due to a fractured fibula he sustained almost two weeks ago. The injury puts him out at least six weeks which does set him up for a return to the playoffs, if they manage to get there in the first place.

Without Maye, it will be former undrafted free agent Tommy DeVito leading the offense that will also be without wideout A.J. Brown who will miss multiple weeks with a hamstring injury.

At the same time, the Chargers could be without Justin Herbert who is currently in the league’s concussion protocol after self-reporting symptoms following Sunday’s loss. He’ll have to clear every step of the protocol to return this week, but will the Chargers really rush him just to see him play in a meaningless game? content.value:
Justin Herbert self-reported concussion symptoms following the Chargers’ loss to the Jets and the quarterback was subsequently placed in the league’s concussion protocol Sunday night. Herbert now has to progress through the entire protocol in order to play against the Patriots on Sunday and with situations like these, they’re always fluid. Some players find a way to not miss any time while others end up missing more than expected.

Knowing this, the Chargers have to prepare for the reality that second-year UDFA D.J. Uiagalelei will start against the Patriots, marking his first start at the professional level.

Uiagalelei got his first snaps during a regular season game in the team’s lopsided loss to the Texans in Week Nine. He only completed a pair of passes, but one of them did go for a touchdown to Derius Davis in garbage time.

His potential opponent DeVito has a starting record of 3-5 with career totals of 1,490 passing yards and nine touchdowns to four interceptions. In 2026, he’s thrown for one touchdown to one pick with 132 passing yards in three appearances.

Regardless of how this quarterback matchup ends up, it’s probably a good thing the NFL did everyone a favor by flexing this one out of Sunday Night Football.

content.value:
This week, we were joined by Taylor Kyles of our Patriots sister site, Pats Pulpit, to help us preview this week’s game against New England.

It’s officially a battle of backup quarterbacks, so I hope everyone is excited for the absolutely wildcard that this game could be!

Let’s go ahead and dive in!

1.) Drake Maye will not be playing this game after suffering a severe lower leg injury and Tommy DeVito looks to be the guy getting the start. What can you tell us about DeVito and what are your expectations for him in this game?

Tommy DeVito was extended by the Patriots this offseason after being the third quarterback behind Drake Maye and Joshua  in 2025. Unfortunately for New England, DeVito didn’t play up to the new deal against the Lions. The veteran threw a bad interception during a two-minute drill before halftime, failed to target open receivers, and delivered two hospital balls on downfield throws. In fairness, DeVito was under consistent pressure and hadn’t seen significant action in years, but the Patriots will need a much better effort from him this weekend.

While DeVito’s vision and anticipation are questionable, he has enough arm talent to hit the crossers and go routes that made up much of his preseason and training camp menu. He also has solid pocket presence and is athletic enough to make plays with his legs when pressure closes in or plays break down. The biggest thing for DeVito will be taking what the defense gives him and minimizing turnover-worthy throws to keep the offense on schedule.

2.) Obviously this season has not lived up to the preseason expectations that followed this team after a Super Bowl appearance. Where did it all go wrong? Are there any signs that this team can rebound in 2027?

Offensively, the Patriots have simply been hammered by injuries, as Jared Wilson is the only starter who hasn’t missed time due to injury. That injury misfortune was compounded by Drake Maye putting the ball in harm’s way far too often, as well as a fairly mundane and at-times nonexistent rushing attack. The offense has some help coming with LG Alijah Vera-Tucker expected to return from injured reserve. However, how he looks after missing over a month is anyone’s guess, though he’s been impressive when on the field.

Defensively, the Patriots simply haven’t played up to their talent. Carlton Davis missing multiple games with a neck injury hasn’t helped, but the defense has been torched in consecutive weeks against NFC North opponents, including one game where Davis played nearly every snap. The biggest issue has been poor fundamentals, including shaky tackling, a lack of players swarming to the football, inconsistent defensive line play, and miscommunications that have led to coverage busts and big plays. Part of the blame also falls on Zak Kuhr’s scheme, which seems more concerned with deploying disguised zone coverages than letting highly paid CB1 Christian Gonzalez do what he does best: play press man coverage against the opponent’s top receiver as often as possible. There are also wrinkles like safeties defending wide receivers to maintain zone looks, a general abundance of off coverage, and a wide menu of coverages that I’m personally not a fan of and think works to the defense’s detriment at times.

Frankly, this feels like a lost season for the Patriots, especially if the defense continues to struggle against talented, well-coached offenses like the Jaguars, Bears, Packers, and Lions, all of whom had standout performances against New England. For them to rebound in 2027, they’ll need injury luck closer to what they enjoyed in 2025, but also an influx of young talent and a reset in veteran leadership, particularly on defense.

3.) If you were Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, how would you go about attacking this Patriots defense? Where are the weak spots? Which players should the Chargers try to avoid? What about ones to exploit?

First and foremost, I’d challenge the interior defensive line and Christian Gonzalez in the run game. Jahmyr Gibbs had a lot of success cutting into the teeth of the Patriots’ defense on outside zone, and Gonzalez has been shaky in run support when directly targeted. I’d also target backup outside cornerback Charles Woods, who’s struggled against double moves and crafty route runners, and Christian Elliss, whose zone depth has been spotty at times. 

I would avoid running at rookie Gabe Jacas, who has a run stop in every career game and plays with a tremendous motor. In the pass game, while Gonzalez hasn’t played up to his usual standard this season, he’s still one of the league’s best corners, especially when playing press. Marcus Jones also remains one of the most competitive slot corners in the league, even if his turnover numbers are below expectation.

4.) If you were Chargers defensive coordinator Chris O’Leary, how would you try and stop this current Patriots offense? What will the team’s plan be without Drake Maye? How will it differ from their normal style of offense?

I would commit all of my resources to stopping the run and forcing Tommy DeVito to win the game. The Patriots’ run game hasn’t been anything to write home about, but this seems like a reasonable key for both teams in a battle of backup quarterbacks. In obvious passing situations, I’d discourage DeVito from throwing outside and guide him toward the middle of the field. I’d also avoid man coverage and force him to be disciplined with his eyes and anticipate windows. The Patriots’ right guard situation is still unsettled, but the right side has been susceptible to stunts and blitzes, so I’d challenge their communication as often as possible. 

5.) Let’s go ahead and top this off with a few lines on how you see this matchup shaking out. Who do you see coming out on top and what will the final score be?

I think coming off a bye and the embarrassment of back-to-back blowouts will propel the Patriots to a win against a vulnerable opponent, but that’s far from a guarantee. If DeVito avoids egregious mistakes and makes 2-3 plays, and the defense plays up to its usual standard, this should be a fairly comfortable win for New England.

content.value:
The Chargers went and won their first game against the Ravens in Week 11 but followed that with yet another loss this past Sunday against the Jets. They’re now 1-9 with seven games to go.

If the Chargers continue their losing ways, they will stay in the mix for one of the top players in the upcoming draft class. Obviously Ohio State’s Jeremiah Smith is the crown jewel of the group, but will the Bolts truly have a shot at taking Smith if they don’t pick number one overall?

To be quite honest, yes, they could.

Quarterbacks always end up being the biggest priority amongst the league’s worst teams. If the Chargers end up picking at No. 3 — like they do in this new mock at The Athletic — then there’s always going to be a chance that two passers go before them which sets the table for the Bolts picking the Heisman favorite.

In Nick Baumgardner’s latest mock, he has the Titans trading up with the Jets to pick Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker at No. 1. The Miami Dolphins then take Notre Dame’s CJ Carr at No. 2. In this scenario, that’s all it takes for the Bolts to land Smith, who currently has 86 receptions for 1,482 yards and 17 touchdowns through 11 games this year.

Here’s what Baumgardner had to say about the pairing with the Chargers:

“Smith would be like a swim-up bar in the desert for Justin Herbert and the Chargers, who need playmakers more than anyone right now. Jim Harbaugh’s team — specifically, his pass offense (ranked 29th in the NFL) — is floundering. Second-year receiver Tre’ Harris leads the team with 28 catches; 48 other receivers in the league have more. The Bolts are out of power there.”

“As college football’s best player, Smith should win the Heisman Trophy. Though he has the goods to become the first receiver to go No. 1 since Keyshawn Johnson in 1996, a QB or two could bump him (slightly) down the board.”

content.value:
The Chargers unfortunately fell short against the Jets 27-24 on Sunday and dropped to 1-9 on the year with seven games remaining. A miraculous late game run to push for a winning record is now impossible and all of you who held out hope for such a thing can now finally let that one go.

Another loss further reinforced the Chargers as one of the league’s worst. With a chance to get out of the bottom three in the league, the defense unfortunately could not find any decent footing as the Jets went the entire game without a single punt.

Offensively it was a better day for Justin Herbert and that unit, but overall it wasn’t enough to beat a previously 2-win Jets team.

With that said, let’s get into the rankings from Week 12.

NFL.com – #29

“After finally winning a game in Week 10, the Chargers returned to their former selves, minus the crushing turnovers. A remarkably quick game saw just 12 possessions combined between the two teams, and the Chargers didn’t quite value them as much as they should have in Sunday’s loss. A complete lack of urgency while facing a 10-point deficit frustrated everyone taking the time to watch this game and included a sequence of snaps that featured a flea flicker on third-and-2, a speed option run by a quarterback (Justin Herbert) who had already taken too many hits, and a pace that ate up nearly eight minutes of time in the fourth quarter. This is an unserious team that unsurprisingly didn’t regain possession after that marathon scoring drive and might not win another game if it continues operating like this.”

Pro Football Talk – #30

“Will Jim Harbaugh be back for 2027?” – Mike Florio

ESPN – #31

“The best player on the Chargers this season is playing out his rookie deal, so the best candidate for an extension is fairly obvious. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Tuipulotu leads the team with 37 pressures through Sunday. Are the Chargers willing to pay him top edge money, which could be close to $35 million per year? Only time will tell.” – Aaron Schatz

The Athletic – #31

“The sooner this season ends, the better. And this game lasted only 2 hours, 40 minutes, the shortest of the year. The Chargers and Jets had only six possessions apiece Sunday. New York scored on its first five, marking a rare occasion when the defense let down Los Angeles. The Chargers are now next to last in the league in offensive EPA per drive (minus-0.80).” – Josh Kendall and Chad Graff

CBS Sports – #31

“After winning at Baltimore, they were back to being the Chargers again, losing to the Jets. This team has to make changes.”

Sports Illustrated – #31

“On the MMQB pod, Albert Breer breathlessly details the potential death knell in the Jim Harbaugh era: a long, meandering drive to nowhere with the game on the line.” – Conor Orr

Yahoo Sports – #32

“Good thing the Chargers got that win in Week 10. Losing to the Jets on Sunday at home was a strong indication that Los Angeles might not win again.“

“At least there were a couple of decent performances on offense. Omarion Hampton continued to get hot late in the season with 89 rushing yards. Justin Herbert had a 119.3 passer rating. His best mark in a game this season before Sunday was 87.5. Unfortunately, Herbert landed in concussion protocol after the loss. Ladd McConkey has had an injury-filled and unproductive season but he had two touchdowns against the Jets. It’s not much, especially in a loss. But it’s not like there have been many other positives for the Chargers.”

Sporting News – #32

“The Chargers played a clean game for the most part, but still lost to the Jets because of a key stat: Giving up six sacks on Justin Herbert. He’s been dropped 39 times in 10 games, the most in the league. The offensive line injuries continue to have lingering effects.” – Vinnie Iyer
